kings.name: Saul
kings.note: Chosen by lot and anointed; rejected for disobedience (1 Sam 13:13; 15:26) and died at Gilboa. Forty years is Paul's figure (Acts 13:21).

kings.name: David
kings.note: Seven years and six months over Judah at Hebron, thirty-three over all Israel from Jerusalem (2 Sam 5:4–5). Right in the LORD's eyes save in the matter of Uriah (1 Kgs 15:5).

kings.name: Solomon
kings.note: Loved the LORD (1 Kgs 3:3), then his wives turned his heart and he did evil in the LORD's sight (11:4–6). The kingdom divided after him.

kings.name: Rehoboam
kings.note: The kingdom divided at his harsh answer (1 Kgs 12). Shishak of Egypt came up in his fifth year (14:25).

kings.name: Abijah
kings.synchronism: In the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat
kings.note: Called Abijam in Kings. His heart was not perfect with the LORD (15:3); 2 Chronicles 13 records his speech against Jeroboam.

kings.name: Asa
kings.synchronism: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel
kings.note: Did right, as David; the high places were not removed (15:14). Diseased in his feet in old age (15:23).

kings.name: Jehoshaphat
kings.synchronism: In the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel
kings.note: Walked in the way of Asa; the high places remained (22:43). Allied with Ahab at Ramoth-gilead.

kings.name: Jehoram of Judah
kings.synchronism: In the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah
kings.note: Married Ahab's daughter and walked in the way of the house of Ahab (8:18). Reckoned from an earlier association with his father, so his years overlap Jehoshaphat's.

kings.name: Ahaziah of Judah
kings.synchronism: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel
kings.note: Walked in the way of the house of Ahab; killed by Jehu (2 Kgs 9:27).

kings.name: Athaliah
kings.note: The only queen to reign. She destroyed the royal seed except Joash, hidden six years (11:1–3); the text gives no verdict formula, but 2 Chronicles 24:7 calls her wicked.

kings.name: Joash
kings.synchronism: In the seventh year of Jehu
kings.note: Did right all his days while Jehoiada the priest instructed him (12:2); after Jehoiada died he turned aside (2 Chr 24:17–19). Slain by his servants.

kings.name: Amaziah
kings.synchronism: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel
kings.note: Did right, yet not like David (14:3); not with a perfect heart (2 Chr 25:2). He outlived Jehoash of Israel by fifteen years (14:17).

kings.name: Uzziah
kings.synchronism: In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel
kings.note: Called Azariah in Kings. Did right (15:3), but pride led him into the temple and he died a leper (2 Chr 26:16–21). Jotham judged the people meanwhile.

kings.name: Jotham
kings.synchronism: In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel
kings.note: Did right; the high places were not removed (15:34–35).

kings.name: Ahaz
kings.synchronism: In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah
kings.note: Walked in the way of the kings of Israel and made his son pass through the fire (16:3). Isaiah met him in the Syro-Ephraimite crisis (Isa 7).

kings.name: Hezekiah
kings.synchronism: In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel
kings.note: Did right as David; removed the high places (18:3–4). Samaria fell in his sixth year (18:10) and Sennacherib came in his fourteenth (18:13).

kings.name: Manasseh
kings.note: Judah's longest reign and its worst; he rebuilt the high places (21:2–3). 2 Chronicles 33:12–13 records his humbling in Babylon.

kings.name: Amon
kings.note: Walked in his father's ways; his servants conspired and slew him (21:19–23).

kings.name: Josiah
kings.note: Crowned at eight. Found the book of the law in his eighteenth year and reformed the land (22:3–8; 23:25). Slain at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho (23:29).

kings.name: Jehoahaz of Judah
kings.note: Called Shallum in Jeremiah 22:11. Pharaoh Necho deposed him and took him to Egypt. Not Jehoahaz of Israel.

kings.name: Jehoiakim
kings.note: Set on the throne by Necho; Nebuchadnezzar came up in his reign (24:1). Jeremiah's scroll was burned before him (Jer 36).

kings.name: Jehoiachin
kings.note: Surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and was carried to Babylon with Ezekiel; released in the thirty-seventh year of his captivity (25:27). Also called Jeconiah and Coniah.

kings.name: Zedekiah
kings.note: Rebelled against Babylon; Jerusalem fell in his eleventh year and he was blinded and taken to Babylon (25:1–7).

kings.name: Jeroboam
kings.note: Led the ten tribes from Rehoboam and set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan (1 Kgs 12:28–30); his "sin" is the measure of every later king.

kings.name: Nadab
kings.synchronism: In the second year of Asa king of Judah
kings.note: Walked in the way of his father; Baasha killed him and all Jeroboam's house (15:27–29).

kings.name: Baasha
kings.synchronism: In the third year of Asa king of Judah
kings.note: Killed Nadab; Jehu son of Hanani prophesied against him (16:1–4).

kings.name: Elah
kings.synchronism: In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah
kings.note: Killed by Zimri while drunk in Arza's house (16:9–10).

kings.name: Zimri
kings.synchronism: In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah
kings.note: Reigned seven days in Tirzah, then burned the palace over himself when the army besieged it (16:18).

kings.name: Omri
kings.synchronism: In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah
kings.note: Contested at first by Tibni (16:21–22). Bought the hill of Samaria and built the city (16:24). Worse than all before him.

kings.name: Ahab
kings.synchronism: In the thirty and eighth year of Asa king of Judah
kings.note: Married Jezebel and served Baal (16:31). Elijah and Micaiah spoke to him. Killed at Ramoth-gilead (22:34–37).

kings.name: Ahaziah of Israel
kings.synchronism: In the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah
kings.note: Walked in the way of his father and mother and of Jeroboam. Reigned partly with Ahab, partly alone, and died without a son (2 Kgs 1:17).

kings.name: Jehoram of Israel
kings.synchronism: In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah
kings.note: Called Joram. Put away the image of Baal, but clung to Jeroboam's sin (3:2–3). Killed by Jehu (9:24).

kings.name: Jehu
kings.note: Anointed to destroy Ahab's house, and did well in it (10:30); yet took no heed to walk in the law of the LORD and kept Jeroboam's calves (10:29, 31).

kings.name: Jehoahaz of Israel
kings.synchronism: In the twenty and third year of Joash king of Judah
kings.note: Oppressed by Hazael of Syria; he sought the LORD and was given a saviour (13:3–5). Not Jehoahaz of Judah.

kings.name: Jehoash of Israel
kings.synchronism: In the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah
kings.note: Called Joash. Wept over the dying Elisha (13:14). Defeated Amaziah of Judah (14:11–14).

kings.name: Jeroboam II
kings.synchronism: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah king of Judah
kings.note: Restored the border of Israel as Jonah had said (14:25). Amos and Hosea prophesied in his days.

kings.name: Zechariah of Israel
kings.synchronism: In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah
kings.note: Followed after an eleven-year gap, an interregnum on Ussher's reckoning. Shallum killed him; so fulfilling the word given to Jehu (15:12). Not the prophet Zechariah.

kings.name: Shallum of Israel
kings.synchronism: In the nine and thirtieth year of Uzziah king of Judah
kings.note: Reigned a full month in Samaria and was killed by Menahem. The text gives him no verdict. Not Shallum (Jehoahaz) of Judah.

kings.name: Menahem
kings.synchronism: In the nine and thirtieth year of Azariah king of Judah
kings.note: Paid Pul king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver (15:19–20).

kings.name: Pekahiah
kings.synchronism: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah
kings.note: Killed by his captain Pekah in the palace at Samaria (15:25).

kings.name: Pekah
kings.synchronism: In the two and fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah
kings.note: Joined Rezin of Syria in attacking Judah (16:5). Tiglath-pileser took the northern cities in his days; Hoshea killed him (15:29–30).

kings.name: Hoshea
kings.synchronism: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah
kings.note: Israel's last king, evil though not as the kings before him (17:2). Followed nine years without a king on Ussher's reckoning. Shalmaneser took Samaria in his ninth year (17:5–6).

prophets.name: Samuel
prophets.note: Anointed Saul (1 Sam 10:1) and later David (16:13). He judged Israel before the kings; this bar covers his work with them.

prophets.name: Nathan
prophets.note: Gave David the covenant promise, rebuked him over Bathsheba (2 Sam 12) and helped secure Solomon's throne (1 Kgs 1).

prophets.name: Gad
prophets.note: David's seer. He told David to leave the stronghold (1 Sam 22:5) and brought the choice of judgments after the census (2 Sam 24:11–14). Dates are not given.

prophets.name: Ahijah
prophets.note: Tore his garment in twelve pieces to tell Jeroboam of the divided kingdom; as an old man he foretold the end of Jeroboam's house (1 Kgs 14:4–16).

prophets.name: Shemaiah
prophets.note: Forbade Rehoboam to fight Israel (1 Kgs 12:22–24) and explained Shishak's invasion (2 Chr 12:5–7).

prophets.name: Elijah
prophets.note: Foretold the drought to Ahab and contended with the prophets of Baal at Carmel. He was taken up in a whirlwind (2 Kgs 2:11). A writing from him reached Jehoram of Judah (2 Chr 21:12–15).

prophets.name: Micaiah
prophets.note: Alone of Ahab's prophets foretold defeat at Ramoth-gilead, and was imprisoned for it.

prophets.name: Elisha
prophets.note: Succeeded Elijah (2 Kgs 2). Advised Jehoram and Jehoshaphat against Moab, sent a prophet to anoint Jehu (9:1–3), and prophesied to Jehoash on his deathbed (13:14–19).

prophets.name: Jonah
prophets.note: Foretold Jeroboam II's restoration of Israel's border. The dates of his mission to Nineveh are not given; this bar shows the reign the text names.

prophets.name: Amos
prophets.note: A herdman of Tekoa who prophesied against Israel two years before the earthquake. The span is the overlap of the two reigns the book names.

prophets.name: Hosea
prophets.note: Prophesied chiefly to Israel. The span runs from Jeroboam II's reign into Hezekiah's; where it ends is not stated.

prophets.name: Joel
prophets.note: The book names no king and no year, so its date is open; Ussher places it under Uzziah and other readers differ widely. Shown with the uncertainty marked.

prophets.name: Isaiah
prophets.note: Saw the LORD in the year Uzziah died (Isa 6:1); met Ahaz (Isa 7) and Hezekiah (2 Kgs 19:2; 20:1). His last dated act is Sennacherib's invasion; Isa 37:38 records that king's death, later still.

prophets.name: Micah
prophets.note: The Morasthite whose words of judgment on Samaria and Jerusalem Jeremiah's elders recalled under Hezekiah (Jer 26:18).

prophets.name: Obadiah
prophets.note: Against Edom for its part in Jerusalem's fall (Obad 11–14). The book names no king; the date follows from the event it describes.

prophets.name: Nahum
prophets.note: Foretold Nineveh's fall after No-amon's (Nah 3:8). The book names no king; the year here is an estimate between those two events.

prophets.name: Zephaniah
prophets.note: The word of the LORD came to him in the days of Josiah; the exact years within that reign are not given.

prophets.name: Huldah
prophets.note: The prophetess consulted in Josiah's eighteenth year about the book of the law.

prophets.name: Jeremiah
prophets.note: Called in Josiah's thirteenth year and prophesied to the carrying away of Jerusalem in Zedekiah's eleventh. He spoke of Shallum (Jehoahaz) in Jer 22:11 and of Coniah (Jehoiachin) in 22:24.

prophets.name: Habakkuk
prophets.note: Foresaw the rise of the Chaldeans (Hab 1:6). The book names no king; the years are an estimate from its content.

prophets.name: Ezekiel
prophets.note: Carried to Babylon with Jehoiachin; called in the fifth year of that captivity (Ezek 1:2). He spoke of Zedekiah's rebellion (Ezek 17:12–21). His last dated word is the twenty-seventh year (29:17).

prophets.name: Daniel
prophets.note: Taken to Babylon in Jehoiakim's reign (Dan 1:1). He served in Babylon and Persia until at least the third year of Cyrus (10:1), about 535 BC, so this bar runs off the chart.
